title: Building LinkedIn's First Agency Intelligence Reporting System

metrics.label: of LinkedIn Media Solutions Revenue Impacted
Agency QBR Reporting Automated via Python

problem: LinkedIn's agency sales team had no dedicated analytics tooling. While client-direct AEs had dashboards and reporting infrastructure, agency partners, who represent 40% of LinkedIn Media Solutions revenue, were being managed with manual Salesforce exports and large Excel files. There was no way to view an agency's full book of business, track performance by vertical, or identify accounts at risk of churn. Internally, leadership lacked the visibility needed to allocate resources or forecast agency revenue accurately.
strategy: After identifying this as the most critical gap on joining the team, I conducted individual discovery sessions with SMEs across both independent agency and holding company segments to map out their specific needs. From there I built a formal project timeline with defined deliverables, benchmarks, and an estimated completion date, treating it like a product build, not a one-off report.
result: I worked with the Product team to identify the backend data tables needed, then built a SQL script that pulled every agency relationship, their full client roster, industry categories, active LinkedIn products, and total spend history. I surfaced this in a Tableau dashboard with a clean UI, enabling AEs to select any agency and immediately see YoY/QoQ/MoM growth, YTD spend, churn signals, and unmanaged accounts worth prioritizing. The dashboard replaced 20+ manual Salesforce pulls per analysis. A later iteration became the standardized 'Agency QBR' in the form of a PowerPoint delivered quarterly to agency partners and was ultimately automated with Python, significantly reducing lift on both the Insights and Sales teams.
takeaway: This project demonstrated how a cross-functional, product-minded approach to an analytics problem can have outsized business impact. Solving for a segment representing 40% of revenue required more than just technical execution. It required stakeholder alignment, structured project management, and a commitment to building something scalable rather than a one-time fix.
